explain.narrative:
## Project: Inventory Tracker

Use a product code to find an item. Encapsulate quantity changes so stock cannot become negative. Test adding, receiving, selling and looking up products independently.

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failures and state assumptions clearly.

Compile with JDK 21, predict output before running, and test normal, boundary and invalid inputs.

examples.title: Core API
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.Map<String,Integer> stock = new java.util.HashMap<>(); stock.put("PEN", 20); System.out.println(stock.get("PEN")); } }
examples.explanation: Stores product quantity by product code in a Map.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.Map<String,Integer> stock = new java.util.HashMap<>(); stock.put("PEN", 20); stock.put("PEN", stock.get("PEN") - 3); System.out.println(stock.get("PEN")); } }

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int available = 5, requested = 7; System.out.println(requested <= available ? "sale allowed" : "insufficient stock"); } }
examples.explanation: Prevents a sale that would make inventory negative.

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.Map<String,Double> prices = java.util.Map.of("PEN", 2.5, "BOOK", 10.0); System.out.println(prices.get("PEN") * 4 + prices.get("BOOK")); } }
examples.explanation: Calculates inventory value from product prices and quantities.

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.Map<String,Integer> stock = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>(); stock.put("PEN", 20); stock.put("BOOK", 5); System.out.println(stock.keySet()); } }
examples.explanation: Uses LinkedHashMap when predictable insertion order is useful.
